rows.speaker: حفص
rows.claim: Hafs dammas the pronominal h in ansānihi; the author explains this by reference to the underlying vowel pattern, as in the cited Fath reading.
rows.anchor: قوله: { وما أنسانيه } قرأ حفص بضم الهاء. وكذا في قوله:

rows.speaker: الباقون
rows.claim: The other readers kasra the h because it follows a silent yāʾ.
rows.anchor: والباقون بالكسر نظرا إلى اللفظ، فإنها بعد ياء ساكنة.

rows.speaker: حفص
rows.claim: Hafs combines dialects of the pronominal h: he uses an unconnected damma here, a yāʾ connection in 25:69, and follows most readers elsewhere.
rows.anchor: وقد جمع حفص في قراءته بين اللغات في هاء الكناية: فإنه ضم الهاء في

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An adhkurahu is an بدل اشتمال of the pronoun in ansānihi, meaning that he made me forget its remembrance.
rows.anchor: قوله: { أن أذكره } في محل نصب على البدل من هاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One analysis makes ʿajaban the second object of ittakhadha; fī al-baḥr may attach to that verb or be an omitted circumstantial phrase, and the subject may be the fish or Moses.
rows.anchor: قوله: " عجبا " فيه أوجه، أحدها: أنه مفعول ثان

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari treats ʿajaban as the quoted exclamation governed by qāla, with the intervening clause as a parenthesis.
rows.anchor: فقال الزمخشري: " أو قال: عجبا في آخر كلامه تعجبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further analysis takes ʿajaban as a verbal noun governed by an implied verb meaning “he marveled greatly.”
rows.anchor: الثالث: أنه مصدر، فالعامل فيه مقدر تقديره: فتعجب من ذلك عجبا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fourth analysis makes ʿajaban an adjective of an omitted verbal noun governed by ittakhadha; on the last three analyses fī al-baḥr can be the second object.
rows.anchor: الرابع: أنه نعت لمصدر محذوف، ناصبه " اتخذ " ، أي: اتخذ سبيله

rows.speaker: نافع وأبو عمرو والكسائي
rows.claim: They delete the yāʾ of nabghi when stopping but retain it in connected recitation; Ibn Kathir retains it in both positions, while the remaining readers delete it in both, following the written form.
rows.anchor: قوله: { نبغ }: حذف نافع وأبو عمرو والكسائي ياء " نبغي " وقفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the yāʾ would normally remain, its deletion imitates verse endings or is eased by deletion of the relative mā’s resumptive pronoun; the comparable yāʾ in 12:65 is retained by all.
rows.anchor: وكان من حقها الثبوت، وإنما حذفت تشبيها بالفواصل، أو لأن الحذف يؤنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qaṣaṣan may be a circumstantial verbal noun meaning “following their tracks,” an implied verb’s cognate object, or an object of irtaddā because it means “they retraced and followed.”
rows.anchor: قوله: " قصصا " فيه ثلاثة أوجه، أحدها: أنه مصدر في موضع الحال

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisaʾi reads ansānihi with imāla.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الكسائي " أنسانيه " بالإمالة.

rows.speaker: عبد الله
rows.claim: ʿAbd Allah reads an adhkuraka, “that I remind you of it.”
rows.anchor: وعبد الله " أن أذكركه ".

rows.speaker: أبو حيوة
rows.claim: Abu Haywa reads wa-ittikhād sabīlihi, coordinating the verbal noun with the object of adhkurahu.
rows.anchor: وأبو حيوة " واتخاذ سبيله " عطف هذا المصدر على مفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿIlman is the second object of ʿallamnāhu; Abu al-Baqāʾ notes that a verbal noun would instead be taʿlīman, the regular form for a Form II verb.
rows.anchor: قوله: { علما }: مفعول ثان ل " علمناه " ، قال أبو البقاء:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min ladunnā may modify the preceding verb or be an omitted circumstantial phrase describing ʿilman.
rows.anchor: و { من لدنا } يجوز أن يتعلق بالفعل قبله، أو بمحذوف على أنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAlā an tuʿallimani is a circumstantial clause describing the object pronoun in attabiʿuka: Moses follows while seeking instruction.
rows.anchor: قوله: { على أن تعلمن }: في موضع / الحال من الكاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rushdan is the second object of tuʿallimani, not of mimmā ʿullimta; Abu al-Baqāʾ argues that the alternative leaves the relative clause without a resumptive pronoun and would make the verb take three objects.
rows.anchor: قوله: " رشدا " مفعول ثان ل " تعلمني " ، لا لقوله:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The readings of rushd were discussed in al-Aʿrāf, where the source also raises whether rushd and rashad have the same meaning.
rows.anchor: وقد تقدم خلاف القراء في " رشدا " في سورة الأعراف. وهل هما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khubran is either a specification shifted from the agent, with the underlying sense “whose knowledge has not encompassed it,” or a verbal noun equivalent to “he has not fully informed him.”
rows.anchor: قوله: { خبرا }: فيه وجهان، أحدهما: أنه تمييز لقوله " تحط "

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan reads khuburan with two dammas.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن " خبرا " بضمتين.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Treating wa-lā aʿṣī as an independent clause with no syntactic position is possible but, in the author’s view, strained.
rows.anchor: قوله: { ولا أعصي }: فيه أربعة أوجه، أحدها: أنها لا محل لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wa-lā aʿṣī may be coordinated with satājidunī, whose clause is accusative as the object of qāla; the coordination shares that position.
rows.anchor: الثاني: أنها في محل نصب عطفا على " ستجدني " لأنها منصوبة

rows.speaker: الشيخ
rows.claim: The Shaykh says coordination with satājidunī has no syntactic position; the author calls this a mistake because satājidunī itself is accusative under qāla.
rows.anchor: وقال الشيخ: " ويجوز أن يكون معطوفا على " ستجدني " فلا

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari offers coordination either with ṣābiran, yielding “patient and not disobedient,” or with satājidunī.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري: ولا أعصي: في محل النصب عطفا على " صابرا "

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Abu Jaʿfar reads with fatḥ on sīn and lām and a doubled nūn, without hamza; the source refers readers to his earlier discussion in Hūd.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر هنا بفتح السين واللام وتشديد النون من غير همز.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām in li-tughriqa can express purpose or the eventual result.
rows.anchor: قوله: { لتغرق }: في اللام وجهان، أحدهما: هي لام العلة.

rows.speaker: الأخوان
rows.claim: The two Kūfan readers read li-yaghraqa with the ship’s people as nominative subject; the other readers use li-tughriqa, addressing Khidr and making the people its accusative object.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الأخوان: " ليغرق " بفتح الياء من تحت وسكون الغين وفتح الراء، " أهلها " بالرفع

rows.speaker: الحسن وأبو رجاء
rows.claim: Al-Hasan and Abu Rajaʾ use the second reading’s syntax but double the rāʾ.
rows.anchor: والحسن وأبو رجاء كذلك، إلا أنهما شددا الراء.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Safīna has plurals sufun and safāʾin; dropping its feminine ending to mean a collective generic is rare, as in jarra/jarr and ʿimāma/ʿimām. An anonymous poem witnesses safīn.
rows.anchor: وتحذف منها التاء مرادا بها الجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Safīna derives from safn, “to peel,” because it peels through water; bint makhr similarly names something that cuts through water.
rows.anchor: واشتقاقها من السفن وهو القشر؛ لأنها تقشر الماء. كما سميت " بنت مخر "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Imran means a grave or momentous thing, from amura al-amru, “the matter became great”; a cited verse uses imran.
rows.anchor: قوله: " إمرا " شيئا عظيما، يقال: أمر الأمر، أي: عظم وتفاقم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿUsran is the second object of tarhiqnī; arhaqahu means to burden or overwhelm someone with something.
rows.anchor: قوله: { عسرا }: كفعول ثان ل " ترهقني " من أرهقه كذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mā in bimā nasītu may be a verbal noun or a relative pronoun with its resumptive pronoun omitted.
rows.anchor: و " ما " في " بما نسيت " مصدرية أو بمعنى الذي، والعائد

rows.speaker: نافع وابن كثير وأبو عمرو
rows.claim: These readers use zākiya with an alif and a light yāʾ, analyzing it as the ordinary active participle; the others use zakiyya without alif and with doubled yāʾ for emphasis.
rows.anchor: قوله: { زاكية }: قرأ " زاكية " بألف وتخفيف الياء نافع

rows.speaker: الباقون
rows.claim: The remaining readers use zakiyya, a faʿīla form conveying intensification.
rows.anchor: وبدون الألف وتشديد الياء الباقون.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A ghulām is normally a boy who has not reached puberty, but may refer figuratively to a grown man by reference to his earlier age; Layla’s verse uses ghulām for a man handling a spear.
rows.anchor: فقيل: مجازا باعتبار ما كان. ومنه قول ليلى:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another poet also uses ghulām for a grown man, including one who is not a poet when verbally challenged.
rows.anchor: وقال آخر:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative takes ghulām literally from iġlām, associated with coming first or reaching maturity, which applies to a postpubescent person.
rows.anchor: وقيل: بل هو حقيقة لأنه من الإغلام وهو السبق، وذلك إنما يكون

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari explains the conjunctions: ship damage is the conditional result, while killing is included in the condition after the boy’s encounter and qāla aqtalta is its result.
rows.anchor: جعل " خرقها " جزاء للشرط، وجعل " قتله " من جملة الشرط

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the ship was not damaged immediately upon boarding, while the killing immediately followed meeting the boy, explaining the different conjunctions.
rows.anchor: لأن الخرق لم يتعقب الركوب، وقد تعقب القتل لقاء الغلام "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bighayri nafs may modify qatalta, be a circumstantial phrase describing killer or victim, or describe an omitted verbal noun; Abu al-Baqāʾ’s circumstantial analysis is judged very remote.
rows.anchor: قوله: { بغير نفس } فيه ثلاثة أوجه، أحدها: انها متعلقة ب " قتلت ".

rows.speaker: نافع وأبو بكر وابن ذكوان
rows.claim: These readers pronounce nukran with two dammas; the rest use one damma followed by sukūn, treated as dialectal variants or as a base form and its derivative.
rows.anchor: قوله: " نكرا " قرأ نافع وأبو بكر وابن ذكوان بضمتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shayʾan can mean the verbal action, “a grievous coming,” or the object, “a reprehensible deed.”
rows.anchor: و " شيئا ": يجوز أن يراد به المصدر، أي: مجيئا نكرا، وأن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view makes imran more severe than nukran because damaging a ship endangers many lives, unlike killing one person.
rows.anchor: وهل النكر أبلغ من الإمر أو بالعكس. فقيل: الإمر أبلغ؛ لأن قتل أنفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opposing view makes nukran more severe because killing is irreversible, whereas ship damage can be repaired.
rows.anchor: بخلاف خرق السفينة فإنه يمكن تداركه، ولذلك قال: " ألم أقل لك "

rows.speaker: العامة
rows.claim: The common reading uses taṣāḥibnī, Form III; ʿĪsā and Yaʿqūb use the simple verb, while a transmission from Abu ʿAmr and Ubayy uses aṣḥabnī with an omitted object estimated as “yourself.”
rows.anchor: قوله: { فلا تصاحبني }: العامة على " تصاحبني " من المفاعلة.

rows.speaker: أبي
rows.claim: Ubayy also reads “let your knowledge not accompany me,” making the omitted object explicit.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبي " فلا تصحبني علمك " فأظهر المفعول.

rows.speaker: العامة
rows.claim: The common form ladunnī doubles the protective nūn added to preserve the sukūn of ladun, by analogy with minnī and ʿannī.
rows.anchor: قوله: { من لدني } العامة على ضم الدال وتشديد النون.

rows.speaker: نافع
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ reads a single nūn, without the protective nūn; the author treats this reading as evidence against Sibawayh’s prohibition.
rows.anchor: ونافع بتخفيف النون. والوجه فيه: أنه لم يلحق نون الوقاية

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh disallows ladun followed directly by the first-person yāʾ; the author rejects the claim that Nāfiʿ’s nūn is simply original, citing two grammatical objections.
rows.anchor: إلا أن سيبويه منع من ذلك وقال: " لا يجوز أن تأتي ب " لدن "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The light nūn may instead be protective after shortened, sukūn-final lad, with kasra where two sukūns meet, or an original nūn with reduced sukūn like ḍād in ʿuḍud.
rows.anchor: ولكن تحتمل هذه القراءة أن تكون النون فيها أصلية، وأن تكون للوقاية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A poem deletes the nūn from ʿan and min.
rows.anchor: وقد حذفت النون من " عن " و " من " في قوله:

rows.speaker: أبو بكر
rows.claim: Abu Bakr reads the dāl with sukūn and a light nūn, signaling the original ḍamma through ishām; readers differ whether ishām is silent lip movement or a partial audible vowel.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو بكر بسكون الدال وتخفيف النون أيضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The source cross-references the discussion of lā taʾmannā in 12:11 and min ladunhu in this sura.
rows.anchor: وقد تقدم هذا محررا في يوسف عند قوله

rows.speaker: عيسى وأبو عمرو
rows.claim: ʿĪsā and a transmission from Abu ʿAmr read ʿudhran with two dammas.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عيسى وأبو عمرو في رواية " عذرا " بضمتين.

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abu ʿAmr also has an additional transmitted form ʿudhrī, annexed to the speaker’s yāʾ.
rows.anchor: وعن أبي عمرو أيضا " عذري " مضافا لياء المتكلم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min ladunnī modifies balaghta or is an omitted circumstantial phrase describing ʿudhran.
rows.anchor: و { من لدني } متعلق ب " بلغت " ، أو بمحذوف على أنه حال من " عذرا ".

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istatʿamā ahlahā answers the ḥattā idhā clause and means that the two asked the people for food.
rows.anchor: جواب " إذا " ، أي:سألاهم الطعام.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating ahlahā may emphasize by replacing a pronoun with an explicit noun, as in an anonymous poem that repeats al-mawt.
rows.anchor: أحدهما: أنه توكيد من باب إقامة الظاهر مقام المضمر كقوله:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, repetition establishes that they sought food from all the town’s inhabitants, not merely the subset they first encountered.
rows.anchor: والثاني: أنه للتأسيس؛ وذلك أن الأهل المأتيين ليسوا جميع الأهل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An yudayyifūhumā is the object of abaw; most readers use the doubled form from ḍayyafa.
rows.anchor: قوله: { أن يضيفوهما } مفعول به لقوله " أبوا ". والعامة

rows.speaker: الحسن وأبو رجاء وأبو رزين
rows.claim: These readers lighten the verb from aḍāfa, comparable to the paired forms mayyala and amāla.
rows.anchor: والحسن وأبو رجاء وأبو رزين بالتخفيف من: أضافه يضيفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yanqaḍ may be Form VII from a bird’s swooping or from qaḍḍa, small pebbles: the wall wants to crumble into pebble-like pieces; it may instead be Form IV from naqḍ, demolishing a structure.
rows.anchor: قوله: { أن ينقض } مفعول الإرادة. و " انقض " يحتمل أن يكون وزنه

rows.speaker: عبد الله والأعمش
rows.claim: The reading yurid layunqaḍ uses a lām and passive verb; the source compares its construction with yurid Allāhu liyubayyina.
rows.anchor: ويؤيد هذا ما في حرف عبد الله وقراءة الأعمش " يريد لينقض " مبنيا

rows.speaker: أبي
rows.claim: Ubayy has the same passive reading but without the lām, using an as complementizer.
rows.anchor: وما قرأ به ابي كذلك إلا أنه { يريد أن ينقض } بغير لام

rows.speaker: الزهري
rows.claim: Al-Zuhrī reads yanqāḍ with an alif after qāf; al-Fārisī derives it from “I smashed it, so it crumbled,” while Abu al-Baqāʾ compares it to yaḥmār; a light-ḍād form is also reported.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الزهري " أن ينقاض " بألف بعد القاف. قال الفارسي:

rows.speaker: علي وعكرمة
rows.claim: ʿAlī, ʿIkrima, and others read yanqāṣ with ṣād, from “to break”; Ibn Khālawayh describes a tooth splitting lengthwise, and poetry uses munqāṣ and qayṣ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ علي أمير المؤمنين رضي الله عنه وعكرمة في آخرين " ينقاص "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Attributing will to the wall is a widespread metaphor; literal created life or Khidr’s theatrical intention is, in the author’s judgment, strained.
rows.anchor: ونسبة الإرادة إلى الجدار مجاز وهو شائع جدا. ومن أنكر المجاز

rows.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr and Abu ʿAmr read la-ttakhadhta from takhadha; the others read lāttakhadhta with hamzat al-waṣl and doubled tāʾ from ittakhadha.
rows.anchor: قوله: " لاتحذت " قرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو " لتخذت "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The derivation is disputed: the doubled form may derive from akhdh with a substituted tāʾ, or both forms from takhadha; in either reading the verb takes one object because it means “acquire.”
rows.anchor: أم هما من تخذ والتاء أصيلة، ووزنهما فعل وافتعل؟ قولان تقدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Firāq baynī is an expansive adverbial annexation; another view takes bayn as “connection,” supported by a cited but unnamed poet.
rows.anchor: قوله: { فراق بيني }: العامة على الإضافة اتساعا في الظرف. وقيل:

rows.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة
rows.claim: Ibn Abī ʿAbla reads firāqu with tanwīn on the basic form; the second coordinated genitive permits bayn to be annexed to the first term.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي عبلة " فراق " بالتنوين على الأصل. وتكرير المضاف إليه

rows.speaker: ابن وثاب
rows.claim: Ibn Waththāb reads sa-unabbiʾuka with a clear yāʾ in place of hamza.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن وثاب " سأنبيك " بإخلاص الياء بدل الهمزة.

rows.speaker: العامة
rows.claim: The common reading has a light sīn in masākīn; ʿAlī reads the doubled-sīn plural masāk, either one who holds a ship’s sail or a tanner of hides, which the author finds unlikely here and suspects is corruption.
rows.anchor: قوله: { لمساكين }: العامة على تخفيف السين، جمع " مسكين ". وقرأ علي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yaʿmalūn is an adjective describing masākīn.
rows.anchor: و " يعملون " صفة لمساكين.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Warāʾahum may denote place or time and may mean behind them or, in cited usage, in front of them; poems and 14:16 support the latter sense.
rows.anchor: قوله: { ورآءهم ملك } " وراء " هنا قيل: يراد بها المكان.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Cited examples for warāʾ meaning “ahead” include an unnamed poet, Labīd, and Suwwār ibn al-Muḍarrib al-Saʿdī.
rows.anchor: وقول لبيد: 3190- أليس ورائي إن تراخت منيتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghaṣban may be a circumstantial verbal noun, a cognate accusative specifying the seizure, or a purpose accusative, though the last is semantically remote.
rows.anchor: قوله: " غصبا " فيه أوجه، أحدها: أنه مصدر في موضع الحال

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says the intention to damage the ship is semantically delayed after fear of seizure but advanced for emphasis; seizure is not the sole reason, since the ship belongs to poor people.
rows.anchor: فكان حقه أن يتأخر عن السبب فلم قدم عليه؟ قلت: النية به التأخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dual “his parents” uses masculine predominance for father and mother, as in al-qamarān and al-ʿumarān; in 12:100 “parents” can also mean father and aunt.
rows.anchor: قوله: { فكان أبواه مؤمنين }: التثنية للتغليب، يريد: أباه وأمه

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري والجحدري
rows.claim: Abu Saʿīd al-Khudrī and al-Jaḥdarī read muʾminān with dual alif; analyses include a dialect and treating kāna as the particle of شأن.
rows.anchor: وأبو سعيد الخدري والجحدري " مؤمنان " بالألف. وفيه ثلاثة أوجه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers taking kāna’s pronoun as the boy, with “his parents were believers” as predicate; a cited line also illustrates the alternate kāna-shaʾn analysis.
rows.anchor: الثالث: أن في " كان " ضمير الغلام، أي: فكان الغلام والجملة بعده الخبر

rows.speaker: نافع وأبو عمرو
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ and Abu ʿAmr read yudabbilahumā with doubled dāl here and in al-Taḥrīm and al-Qalam; the others use Form IV in all three places.
rows.anchor: قوله: { أن يبدلهما }: قرأ نافع وأبو عمرو بفتح الباء وتشديد الدال

rows.speaker: ثعلب
rows.claim: Thaʿlab distinguishes ibdāl, removing one jewel and replacing it, from tabdīl, changing the form while the same jewel remains; his verse witnesses mubaddal.
rows.anchor: وأنشد: 3193- عزل الأمير للأمير المبدل

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ cites 25:70 for the distinction; the author says Thaʿlab’s distinction is sound but Arabic also uses abdalta for baddalta.
rows.anchor: واحتج الفراء بقوله تعالى: يبدل الله سيئاتهم حسنات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lexical issue bears on 14:48: interpreters disagree whether the earth itself changes or only its attributes.
rows.anchor: قلت: ومن ثم اختلف الناس في قوله تعالى:

rows.speaker: ابن عامر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir reads ruhuman with two dammas; the others use one damma and one sukūn, both meaning mercy.
rows.anchor: قوله: " رحما " قرأ ابن عامر " رحما " بضمتين.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reads raḥiman, supporting “kinship,” apt to the birth relation; Ruʾba’s poem witnesses the mercy sense.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الرحم بمعنى الرحم. وهو لائق هنا من أجل القرابة بالولادة. ويؤيده قراءة ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zakātan and raḥman are accusative specifications.
rows.anchor: و " زكاة ورحما " منصوبان على التمييز.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Raḥmatan is most clearly a purpose accusative; alternatives take it as a circumstantial description of God or a cognate accusative because the sense is “He showed them mercy.”
rows.anchor: قوله: { رحمة }: فيه ثلاثة أوجه، أوضحها: أنه مفعول له.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tasṭaʿ has competing derivations: deletion of a Form VIII tāʾ, deletion/replacement involving ṭāʾ (judged far-fetched), or an added sīn compensating for wāw becoming alif; Ibn al-Sikkīt records four forms.
rows.anchor: قوله: تسطع " ، قيل: أصله استطاع

rows.speaker: ابن السكيت
rows.claim: Ibn al-Sikkīt records istatāʿa with two tāʾs and istāʿa with one, completing four attested forms.
rows.anchor: ويقال: " استتاع " بتاءين، و " استاع " بتاء واحدة، فهذه أربع لغات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhikran means an account of Dhū al-Qarnayn’s reports and stories.
rows.anchor: قوله: { منه ذكرا }: أي: من أخباره وقصصه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object of makkannā is omitted and understood as his affairs, authority, and what he wished to do.
rows.anchor: قوله: { إنا مكنا له }: مفعوله محذوف، أي: أمره وما يريد.

rows.speaker: نافع وابن كثير وأبو عمرو
rows.claim: These readers use ittabaʿa with hamzat al-waṣl and doubled tāʾ in all three occurrences; the others read atbaʿa with hamza and a quiescent tāʾ.
rows.anchor: قوله: { فأتبع }: قرأ نافع وابن كثير وأبو عمرو " فأتبع " و " ثم أتبع "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One analysis treats the readings as synonyms taking one object; another makes Form IV transitive to two objects with one omitted, as in 28:42 and 26:60.
rows.anchor: فقيل: هما بمعنى واحد فيتعديان لمفعول واحد. وقيل: " أتبع " بالقطع

rows.speaker: أبو عبيد
rows.claim: Abu ʿUbayd prefers ittabaʿa because it describes traveling along a route; atbaʿa instead means catching up, as in 37:10.
rows.anchor: واختار أبو عبيد " اتبع " بالوصل، قال: " لأنه من المسير "

rows.speaker: يونس وأبو زيد
rows.claim: Yūnus and Abu Zayd say Form IV conveys rapid, urgent pursuit, while Form VIII means following a trail without that added force.
rows.anchor: وقال يونس وأبو زيد: " أتبع " بالقطع عبارة عن المجد المسرع

rows.speaker: ابن عامر وأبو بكر والأخوان
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir, Abu Bakr, and the two Kūfan readers read ḥāmiyah, an active participle meaning hot; Abu ʿUbayd prefers this because Companions read it.
rows.anchor: قوله: { حامية }: قرأ ابن عامر وأبو بكر والأخوان بالألف وياء ضريحة

rows.speaker: الباقون
rows.claim: The remaining readers read ḥamiʾah, from ḥamaʾa, “mud.”
rows.anchor: والباقون دون ألف وهمزة بعد الميم. فأما القراءة الأولى فإنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās corrected Muʿāwiya’s ḥāmiyah to ḥamiʾah; Ibn ʿUmar agreed with Muʿāwiya, while Kaʿb described water and mud, supporting Ibn ʿAbbās; a verse by Tubbaʿ also depicts a muddy spring.
rows.anchor: وكان ابن عباس عند معاوية. فقرأ معاوية " حامية " فقال ابن عباس: " حمئة "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two readings do not conflict: the spring may be both hot and muddy.
rows.anchor: ولا تناقض بين القراءتين؛ لأن العين جامعة بين الوصفين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An tuʿadhdhiba may be nominative as a subject with omitted predicate or predicate of an implied subject; it may instead be accusative under an implied verb meaning “to punish.”
rows.anchor: قوله: { إمآ أن تعذب } يجوز في { أن تعذب } الرفع على الابتداء

rows.speaker: الأخوان وحفص
rows.claim: The two Kūfan readers and Ḥafṣ read jazāʾan accusative with tanwīn; the others read it nominative annexed to al-ḥusnā.
rows.anchor: قوله: { جزآء الحسنى }: قرأ الأخوان وحفص بنصب " جزاء " وتنوينه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Accusative jazāʾan may be an emphatic verbal noun under an implied or cognate verb, making the clause parenthetical; although its placement is disputed, inserting it between topic and predicate seems more likely.
rows.anchor: فالنصب على المصدر المؤكد لمضمون الجملة، فتنصب بمضمر أو مؤكد لعامل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another analysis takes accusative jazāʾan as circumstantial; the nominative reading makes it a subject with the preceding prepositional phrase as predicate, and al-ḥusnā genitive.
rows.anchor: الثالث: أنه في موضع الحال. والقراءة الثانية رفعه فيها على الابتداء

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ analyzes the accusative as specification (tamyīz), which the author considers remote.
rows.anchor: الرابع: نصبه على التفسير. قاله الفراء. يعني التمييز. وهو بعيد.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومسروق
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Masrūq read accusative with annexation, either supplying an omitted subject (“the reward is the reward of the best”) or deleting tanwīn before another sukūn, as in a cited poem.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس ومسروق بالنصب والإضافة. وفيها تخريجان

rows.speaker: عبد الله وابن أبي إسحاق
rows.claim: They read jazāʾ nominative with tanwīn as a subject; al-ḥusnā may be apposition, clarification, an object of implied aʿnī, or predicate of an implied subject.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله وابن أبي إسحاق " جزاء " مرفوعا منونا على الابتداء

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Abu Jaʿfar reads yusran with a damma wherever it occurs; yusran modifies an omitted verbal noun, “a saying made easy.”
rows.anchor: و " يسرا " نعت مصدر محذوف، أي: قولا ذا يسر. وقرأ أبو جعفر

rows.speaker: العامة
rows.claim: The common reading has kasra on the lām of maṭliʿ despite the usual fatha in this noun when the present verb has ḍamma; other verbs preserve this kasra by attested usage.
rows.anchor: قوله: { مطلع }: العامة على كسر اللام، والمضارع يطلع بالضم

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisāʾī says the dialect with kasra in both the present verb and noun has died out.
rows.anchor: قال الكسائي: " هذه اللغة قد ماتت " يعني: أي: بكسر اللام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In kadhālika, the kāf may be nominative (“the matter was thus”) or accusative (“we acted in that manner”).
rows.anchor: قوله: { كذلك }: الكاف: إما مرفوعة المحل، أي: الأمر كذلك.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For balagha bayna al-saddayn, bayna may be an adverb with the object omitted (“he reached his goal”) or an expanded direct object meaning the place between the two barriers.
rows.anchor: " بين " هنا يجوز أن يكون طرفا، والمفعول محذوف، أي: بلغ غرضه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Readers vary the sīn vowel in saddayn and sadd across this sura and Yā Sīn. Some treat the forms as synonyms; the divine-made versus human-made distinction is rejected by counterexamples, and al-Khalīl’s noun/source distinction is preferred.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو بفتح سين " السدين " و " سدا " في هذه السورة

rows.speaker: الأخوان
rows.claim: The two Kūfan readers use Form IV with ḍamma on yāʾ and kasra on qāf, meaning “they could not make others understand,” with the object omitted.
rows.anchor: قوله: { يفقهون }: قرأ الأخوان بضم الياء وكسر القاف من أقفه

rows.speaker: الباقون
rows.claim: The other readers use the active form: the people themselves scarcely understand others’ speech. The readings are close but not logically equivalent in both directions.
rows.anchor: والباقون بفتحها، أي: لا يفهمون كلام غيرهم، وهو بمعنى الأول

rows.speaker: عاصم
rows.claim: ʿĀṣim reads Yaʾjūj and Maʾjūj with a quiescent hamza; the others use a plain alif. They may be foreign names or Arabic-derived words with competing etymologies and forms.
rows.anchor: قوله: { يأجوج ومأجوج }: قرأ عاصم بالهمزة الساكنة، والباقون بألف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Proposed Arabic roots include blazing fire, intense heat or commotion, rapid running, and salty water; Ruʾba’s verse witnesses taʾujju and the names’ possible patterns.
rows.anchor: وقيل: بل هما عربيان واختلفوا في اشتقاقهما: فقيل: اشتقاقهما من أجيج النار

rows.speaker: أبو حاتم
rows.claim: Abu Ḥātim derives Maʾjūj from māja yamūju, “to surge,” as mafʿūl from underlying mawjūj; the author questions the unusual change of a quiescent weak radical.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون ماجوج من ماج يموج، أي: اضطرب ومنه الموج

rows.speaker: رؤبة وأبوه العجاج
rows.claim: Ruʾba and his father al-ʿAjjāj read Ājūj; the hamza is identified as a dialect of Banū Asad.
rows.anchor: والهمزة في يأجوج ومأجوج لغة بني أسد. وقرأ رؤبة وأبوه العجاج

rows.speaker: ابن عامر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir reads kharjan with sukūn on rāʾ here and in 23:72; the Kūfan pair use kharājan in both places, and other readers mix forms. The words may be synonyms or distinguish annual land tax from one-time payment.
rows.anchor: قوله: " خراجا " قرأ ابن عامر " خرجا " هنا وفي المؤمنين
